title: Green lights are not end-to-end proof
learningClaim: The learner distinguishes a physical Ethernet link from IPv4 reachability between two nodes.

scenario.initialState: Two nodes are connected by one link. Both interfaces report link-up, but neither interface has an IPv4 address.
scenario.learnerTask: Predict, observe, and explain whether the nodes can reach one another before and after IPv4 addresses are assigned.
environmentNotes: A hardware run can expose carrier, speed, duplex, and Ethernet padding.
A virtual veth run preserves separate Linux network stacks but not physical-layer behavior.

evidenceStages.prompt: Both Ethernet ports show a green link light. Does that prove a ping between the nodes will succeed? Explain your prediction.
expectedEvidence: The learner states that link-up alone does not prove IP reachability.
The learner identifies addressing or routing as a separate requirement.

evaluation.passCondition: The response separates physical link state from end-to-end IP communication.

evidenceStages.prompt: Inspect the interfaces and attempt the ping before assigning IPv4 addresses. What is present, and what is missing?
expectedEvidence: The interface is operational at the link layer.
No usable IPv4 address or route exists for the target.
The ping does not establish reachability.

evaluation.passCondition: System state confirms link-up and absent IPv4 configuration; the learner identifies both.

evidenceStages.prompt: Why can the physical connection be healthy while the ping still fails?
expectedEvidence: The explanation treats physical connectivity and network-layer identity as different conditions.
The explanation does not blame the cable merely because ping failed.

evaluation.passCondition: The causal explanation distinguishes what has been proven from what has not.

evidenceStages.prompt: A new pair of machines shows link-up, and both have IPv4 addresses, but they are configured on incompatible subnets with no router. What should you inspect next, and why?
expectedEvidence: The learner does not return to Layer 1 as the first diagnosis.
The learner inspects address prefixes and routing because the changed case already establishes link state.

evaluation.passCondition: The learner transfers the layered model to a changed failure rather than repeating the original command sequence.

successRule.reviewPolicy: All required stages need evidence. Any ambiguous explanation remains review rather than being silently promoted to pass.

provenance.author: max-edtech
provenance.notes: Independent synthetic evidence example inspired by the upstream lesson. No upstream scripts, learner records, or packet captures are redistributed.
